Known:

- Service Orion returned HTTP 503 once.
- A later health check returned HTTP 200.
- This suggests the later health check succeeded, but does not establish when or why the earlier failure occurred.

Unknown:

- Whether the 503 was transient or recurring.
- The timing, duration, and cause of the 503.
- Whether dependencies were unavailable or degraded.
- Whether real user request paths were affected.
- Whether the service is currently healthy beyond that single 200 response.
- Whether any configuration, deployment, infrastructure, or network event was involved.

Next read-only checks:

- Review the timestamps and response details for both checks.
- Inspect existing service and platform logs around the 503 timeframe.
- Check dependency health and recent dependency errors.
- Exercise representative user-facing request paths without changing data.
- Review read-only monitoring, uptime, deployment, and infrastructure event history.
- Repeat health and user-path checks over time to determine whether the issue recurs.
